terra.problem: Remembering a day does not necessarily mean celebrating it. The explanation sets up a misleading contrast.
The claim that nobody would be conceived on an erased night goes beyond what Job says.
Job asks for no joyful voice, not for complete silence or the absence of every happy sound.
The explanation says nobody is cheering, presenting Job's wish as an established fact.
The text does not say Job was sleepless for seven days.
It states without qualification that Job finds this detail comforting. The text does not say that.
Comparing captivity and oppression to a boss's phone call makes light of a serious situation.
Calling the scene a picture of fairness presents an assessment the text does not make as Job's whole point.
Being freed from a master is not necessarily the opposite of being punished. The contrast is misleading.
The claim that ordinary things have lost their sparkle generalizes beyond Job's statement about sighing when food is set before him.
